$comment: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for 'can this change reach a shipped binary?' (Story 16.36).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The same allow-list used to live twice, as `on.push.paths` in
ios-release.yml and android-release.yml, and the two copies had already drifted apart:
neither listed `modules/**`, so a change to the local Expo module modules/wear-data-layer/
triggered no build at all. nightly-builds.yml would have been a THIRD copy, and the worst
one — GitHub applies `paths:`/`paths-ignore:` only to the push and pull_request events, so a
`schedule:` run gets no path filtering whatsoever and has to compute the decision itself.
A stale entry in an unattended 03:00 job means 'we quietly stopped shipping'.
WHY THE DUPLICATION IS STILL THERE. `on.push.paths` cannot reference an external file. So
the duplication is irreducible and is instead made LOUD: `yarn check:build-path-filters`
fails when either release workflow's `on.push.paths` disagrees with this file. Edit here
first, then mirror into the workflow the guard names.
ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. GitHub resolves these per file by LAST match wins, so a negative
pattern after a positive one excludes that path, while a commit that ALSO touches real
source still matches and still builds. `excludes` is therefore appended last to every set.
JSON, not YAML, on purpose: no YAML parser is a declared dependency of this repo, and every
script under scripts/ imports node builtins only. JSON.parse is one.
`$comment` keys are documentation and are stripped by loadFilterConfig().
Shared verbatim with ios-release.yml's `on.push.paths`, and with the nightly's iOS set.
One iOS build ships three targets — the phone app, the watchOS app and the WidgetKit
complication — because Apple has no standalone watchOS upload (ADR-2026-04-11-002).
catalogue/** is here because watch-ios/Scripts/generate-catalogue.swift reads
catalogue/italy.json during the build, so a brand added to the catalogue alone still
changes what ships.
Shared verbatim with android-release.yml's `on.push.paths`, and with the nightly's
Android set. targets/** and watch-ios/** are DELIBERATELY absent: the watch companion is
iOS-only. watch-android/** is deliberately absent too, but only from the release
workflow — see nightlyExtra.
modules/** is here for the obvious reason (modules/wear-data-layer is the phone-side Wear
transport) and is ALSO in the iOS list for a less obvious one: core/wear-connectivity.ts
does `require('@/modules/wear-data-layer')`, so the module's TypeScript is bundled for
both platforms even though its native half is Android-only.
NIGHTLY ONLY, and the asymmetry is deliberate. `fastlane android adhoc` builds no Wear
artifact, so a Wear-only change must NOT trigger android-release.yml — but the nightly
ships the Wear AAB, so it must. The nightly makes ONE Android decision over the union of
the phone and Wear sets, keeping Story 16.35's stance that the two artifacts are one
release intent and a partial ship should be one red X, not two green ones.
Added to BOTH platforms' nightly sets, replacing the per-workflow self-reference the
release workflows carry. A change to the nightly pipeline or to this config should produce
a nightly build, for the same reason ios-release.yml lists itself: so a pipeline change is
exercised rather than merely merged.
Appended LAST to every set. Files that cannot reach a binary: tests are co-located beside
their subject and stories are Storybook-only (Chromatic covers those, and there is no web
target). A commit that also touches real source still builds.
